text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London edged higher in late trading, dragging further forward positions higher and boosting the already solid turnover. August closed $2.70 higher at $323.90 per tonne. October was up $2.50 at $313.00 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York closed a dull session higher although most active July failed to rally above resistance. July added 3 points to close at 11.21 cents/lb, while October closed 6 points higher at 11.01 cents/lb. Our third estimate of world sugar production 1996/97 had no discernible impact as it was in line with expectations.

RUSSIA - Sugar beet sowing in Russia reached 890,000 ha by May 26, 12.5 percent down from the 1,017,000 ha sown last year. The total area sown to beet this season is forecast to fall to 1.065 million ha, down from 1.071 million ha last year.

SOUTH KOREA - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 122,096 tonnes, raw value, slightly up on the 121,679 tonnes imported in December 1995. This brought total imports in calendar year 1996 up to 1.399 million tonnes against 1.306 million tonnes in 1995 and 1.275 million tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in 1996 were Thailand with 628,656 tonnes against 364,321 tonnes, Australia with 621,595 tonnes, down from 664,155 tonnes and South Africa with 109,899 tonnes against 150,445 tonnes. Sugar exports in December 1996 reached 33,540 tonnes, up on 13,391 tonnes in December 1995.

This brought cumulative exports in 1996 up to 300,637 tonnes, sharply up on last year's 247,235 tonnes and the 1994 result of 297,572 tonnes. Major countries of destination in 1996 were Hong Kong with 135,909 tonnes whites against 119,973 tonnes, Indonesia with 59,446 tonnes, up from 37,249 tonnes and Saudi Arabia with 26,048 tonnes against nil.

AUSTRALIA - According to preliminary figures, raw sugar exports in April 1997 amounted to 144,505 tonnes, down from 169,289 tonnes in April 1996. Major countries of destination in April 1997 were Malaysia with 31,500 tonnes compared to 17,848 tonnes, Japan with 38,000 tonnes, up from 16,630 tonnes, Taiwan with 31,500 tonnes against 32,934 tonnes and Singapore with 20,022 tonnes against nil.

ROMANIA - Sugar imports in January 1997 amounted to 10,063 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 3,757 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996/97 (September/January) to 152,029 tonnes, more than twice as much as last year's 60,617 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 327,159 tonnes against 275,178 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Brazil with 87,499 tonnes whites against 21,000 tonnes, Moldova with 15,041 tonnes against 10,199 tonnes and Austria with 11,315 tonnes compared to 6,941 tonnes. At 246,000 tonnes, raw value, total production in 1996/97 was up by 30,000 tonnes against the 1995/96 result.

Dutch sugar firm Limako said it had been awarded a tender by the European Commission to supply 400 tonnes of white sugar as food aid to Angola. The price was 329.50 ECUs per tonne free at port of Amsterdam. The shipment is part of the Rome- based world food programme. The European Union awarded 64,275 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 42.874 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on May 28. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to May 28 reached 2,097,875 tonnes, which compares to 2,212,448 tonnes last year.
